entries.title: Draft: exact three-state mean-field minimax barrier
entries.statement: AUTHOR PROOF; INDEPENDENT REVIEW PENDING. For S={x_i>=0,sum x_i=1}, F_J(x)=sum x_i log x_i-(J/2)sum x_i^2 (0 log 0=0), and J0=4 log 2, the global minimizers are u=(1/3,1/3,1/3) and permutations of v=(2/3,1/6,1/6). The infimum over continuous paths u to v of their maximum F_J0 excess above the global minimum is exactly Delta=log 3-(19/12)log 2>0, attained via (1/2,1/4,1/4). This is a mean-field auxiliary result; C0048 and novelty remain unverified.

entries.title: Draft: sharp obstruction to an approximation-only jump bridge
entries.statement: AUTHOR PROOF; INDEPENDENT REVIEW PENDING. Let S={x_i>=0,sum_{i=1}^3 x_i=1}, F_J(x)=sum x_i log x_i-(J/2)sum x_i^2 with 0 log 0=0, J0=4 log 2, u=(1/3,1/3,1/3), v=(2/3,1/6,1/6), and Delta=log 3-(19/12)log 2. The sublevel {F_J0<=min_S F_J0+epsilon} contains a continuous path u to v iff epsilon>=Delta. For every epsilon>Delta, choose 0<h<min(J0,3(epsilon-Delta)); x(m)=((1+2m)/3,(1-m)/3,(1-m)/3) with m(J) linear from 0 to 1/2 across [J0-h,J0+h] obeys F_J(x(m(J)))-min_S F_J<=Delta+|J-J0|/3<epsilon continuously. This inequality alone cannot force a jump. The selector is not asserted to be a lattice Gibbs magnetization.

entries.title: Draft: normalized error obstruction for the q=3 mean-field route
entries.statement: AUTHOR DERIVATION; INDEPENDENT REVIEW PENDING. In Biskup-Chayes Main Theorem (1.12), the q=3 rescaled Potts inner product gives n=2,kappa=2/3 and allowance E_d(J0)=(2J0/3)I_d, where J0=4 log 2, a(k)=d^(-1)sum cos(k_j), and I_d=integral a^2/(1-a) under normalized torus measure. For integer d>=3, symmetry gives I_d>=1/(2d). Hence E_3(J0)>=4 log 2/9, more than 272.8 times Delta=log 3-(19/12)log 2. E_d(J0)<Delta is impossible for d<=818; d=819 passing this necessary lower-bound test is not sufficient. This bounds a theorem allowance, not actual Gibbs error or the lattice dimension at which discontinuity begins.
assumptions: probability-vector normalization F_J=sum x_i log x_i-(J/2)sum x_i^2

entries.title: Draft: a jump location needs identification with the first critical point
entries.statement: SOURCE-SCOPE DRAFT; INDEPENDENT REVIEW PENDING. C0048 asks for positive color-boundary spontaneous magnetization at the first critical point of the standard nearest-neighbor zero-field Potts model on Z^d for every integer q>=3,d>=3. The cited Biskup-Chayes Theorem 2.1 proves a jump at J_t near J_MF in sufficiently large d, while its following paragraph explicitly does not establish m_*(J)=0 for every J<J_t. Invoking that theorem alone requires an additional argument identifying J_t=J_c to obtain the first-critical-point claim. This does not assess other large-d results; current C0048 openness is UNKNOWN.
assumptions: C0048 uses critical spontaneous magnetization, not arbitrary secondary jumps

relations.rationale: The exact minimax barrier proves both the absence below Delta and the explicit connecting path at Delta.
The normalized Biskup-Chayes allowance is compared with the exact Delta separating the three-state mean-field minima.
Both delimit what the same mean-field theorem can certify: error size and identification of the jump with first criticality are separate missing inputs.
